From the courts into the temple

After Ezekiel had examined the courts, he was brought inside the temple.

When we pay careful attention to the clearer parts of religion, follow their instructions and benefit from them, we will be led into a deeper understanding of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven.
classic_reading:
[Ezek.41.1]
Chapter 41
After the prophet had observed the courts, he was brought to the temple. If we attend to instructions in the plainer parts of religion, and profit by them, we shall be led further into an acquaintance with the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven.

The priests' rooms and private devotion

This chapter describes the rooms for the priests, their purpose, and the dimensions of the holy mountain on which the temple stood.

There were many rooms.

Jesus said that in his Father's house are many dwelling places.

Even in God's house on earth there are many: multitudes have found a home in his sanctuary through faith, and yet there is still room.

These rooms were private, but they stood near the temple.

Similarly, our private acts of worship and prayer should prepare us for public worship and help us benefit more fully from it as circumstances permit.
classic_reading:
[Ezek.42.1]
Chapter 42
In this chapter are described the priests' chambers, their use, and the dimensions of the holy mount on which the temple stood. These chambers were many. Jesus said, In my Father's house are many mansions: in his house on earth there are many; multitudes, by faith, are lodging in his sanctuary, and yet there is room. These chambers, though private, were near the temple. Our religious services in our chambers, must prepare for public devotions, and further us in improving them, as our opportunities are.

The glory of God and the sacrifice of Christ

After Ezekiel had surveyed God's temple, he saw the glory of God.

When the Holy Spirit shows us Christ crucified and the gifts God freely gives us through him, we become ashamed of our sins.

That humility prepares us to understand more deeply the mysteries of redeeming love.

All of Scripture should be opened and applied so that people recognize their sins and repent.

We are not now to offer sacrifices to atone for sin.

Through one offering, Christ has perfected forever those who are being sanctified (Hebrews 10:14).

Nevertheless, we still need the sprinkling of his blood whenever we approach God the Father.

Even our best acts of worship and service are acceptable to him only through the blood that cleanses us from every sin.
classic_reading:
[Ezek.43.1]
Chapter 43
After Ezekiel had surveyed the temple of God, he had a vision of the glory of God. When Christ crucified, and the things freely given to us of God, through Him, are shown to us by the Holy Ghost, they make us ashamed for our sins. This frame of mind prepares us for fuller discoveries of the mysteries of redeeming love; and the whole of the Scriptures should be opened and applied, that men may see their sins, and repent of them. We are not now to offer any atoning sacrifices, for by one offering Christ has perfected for ever those that are sanctified, Heb. 10:14; but the sprinkling of his blood is needful in all our approaches to God the Father. Our best services can be accepted only as sprinkled with the blood which cleanses from all sin.

Christ enters by his own righteousness

This chapter contains instructions concerning the true priests.

Henry understands the prince to mean Christ.

The words of Ezekiel 44:2 remind us that no one else can enter heaven, the true sanctuary, in the way Christ did.

He entered by virtue of his own excellence, personal holiness, righteousness and strength.

He is the brightness of Jehovah's glory and entered by his own holiness.

But that way of entering is closed to everyone else.

We must all come as sinners, by faith in Christ's blood and through the power of his grace.
classic_reading:
[Ezek.44.1]
Chapter 44
This chapter contains ordinances relative to the true priests. The prince evidently means Christ, and the words in [Ezek.44.2] Ezek 44:2, may remind us that no other can enter heaven, the true sanctuary, as Christ did; namely, by virtue of his own excellency, and his personal holiness, righteousness, and strength. He who is the Brightness of Jehovah's glory entered by his own holiness; but that way is shut to the whole human race, and we all must enter as sinners, by faith in his blood, and by the power of his grace.

Justice, worship and Christ our Passover

In the period foretold here, God's worship and its ministers will be provided for.

Rulers will govern justly, recognizing that their authority is held under Christ.

The people will enjoy peace, ease and godliness.

Henry says these promises seem to be expressed in images drawn from the customs of Ezekiel's own time.

Christ is our Passover sacrifice, offered for us.

We celebrate the remembrance of that sacrifice in the Lord's Supper, our Passover feast.

There we rejoice in deliverance from the Egyptian bondage of sin and preservation from the destroying sword of God's justice.

Indeed, the whole Christian life is—and must remain—a feast of unleavened bread, lived in sincerity and truth.
classic_reading:
[Ezek.45.1]
Chapter 45
In the period here foretold, the worship and the ministers of God will be provided for; the princes will rule with justice, as holding their power under Christ; the people will live in peace, ease, and godliness. These things seem to be represented in language taken from the customs of the times in which the prophet wrote. Christ is our Passover that is sacrificed for us: we celebrate the memorial of that sacrifice, and feast upon it, triumphing in our deliverance out of the Egyptian slavery of sin, and our preservation from the destroying sword of Divine justice, in the Lord's supper, which is our passover feast; as the whole Christian life is, and must be, the feast of the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

Worship and Christian freedom

This chapter describes the appointed worship of the prince and the people and the gifts the prince may give to his sons and servants.

Our Lord has commanded us to perform many duties.

But he has also left many matters to our choice.

Those who delight in his commandments may do more than the minimum for his glory, without binding their own consciences unnecessarily or imposing unsuitable rules on others.

Yet this freedom must never become an excuse to neglect daily worship.

Nor may we fail to apply the sacrifice of the Lamb of God to our own souls for pardon, peace and salvation.
classic_reading:
[Ezek.46.1]
Chapter 46
The ordinances of worship for the prince and for the people, are here described, and the gifts the prince may bestow on his sons and servants. Our Lord has directed us to do many duties, but he has also left many things to our choice, that those who delight in his commandments may abound therein to his glory, without entangling their own consciences, or prescribing rules unfit for others; but we must never omit our daily worship, nor neglect to apply the sacrifice of the Lamb of God to our souls, for pardon, peace, and salvation.

Living waters, the gospel and the Spirit

The waters in Ezekiel's vision signify the gospel of Christ.

It went out from Jerusalem into neighboring countries and spread still farther.

They also picture the gifts and powers of the Holy Spirit that accompanied the gospel and enabled it to spread and bear blessed fruit.

Christ is the Temple and the Door.

The living waters flow from him, from his pierced side.

The waters grow deeper as they flow.

Notice both the gospel's progress in the world and grace's growth in the believer's heart.

Pay attention to the Holy Spirit's work under divine guidance.

When we examine God's truth, some matters are clear and easy to understand, like water reaching the ankles.

Others call for deeper investigation, like water reaching the knees or the waist.

Still others lie beyond our understanding, where we can only worship God for the depths of his wisdom, as Paul did (Romans 11).

It is wise to begin with what is most easily understood before going on to difficult and obscure subjects.

Where the gospel is preached, the promises of Scripture and the privileges of believers are made abundant in their souls by the life-giving Spirit.

They nourish and delight the heart, and never wither, fade or run dry.

Even the leaves serve as medicine.

The warnings and rebukes of God's word may be less pleasant than its consolations, but they help heal spiritual disease.

Everyone who believes in Christ and is united to him through his sanctifying Spirit shares in the privileges belonging to Israel.

There is room in the church and in heaven for all who seek the blessings of the new covenant, whose Mediator is Christ.
classic_reading:
[Ezek.47.1]
Chapter 47
These waters signify the gospel of Christ, which went forth from Jerusalem, and spread into the countries about; also the gifts and powers of the Holy Ghost which accompanied it, by virtue of which is spread far, and produced blessed effects. Christ is the Temple; and he is the Door; from him the living waters flow, out of his pierced side. They are increasing waters. Observe the progress of the gospel in the world, and the process of the work of grace in the heart; attend the motions of the blessed Spirit under Divine guidance. If we search into the things of God, we find some things plain and easy to be understood, as the waters that were but to the ankles; others more difficult, which require a deeper search, as the waters to the knees, or the loins; and some quite beyond our reach, which we cannot penetrate; but must, as St. Paul did, adore the depth, Rom. 11. It is wisdom to begin with that which is most easy, before we proceed to that which is dark and hard to be understood. The promises of the sacred word, and the privileges of believers, as shed abroad in their souls by the quickening Spirit, abound where the gospel is preached; they nourish and delight the souls of men; they never fade nor wither, nor are exhausted. Even the leaves serve as medicines to the soul: the warnings and reproofs of the word, though less pleasant than Divine consolations, tend to heal the diseases of the soul. All who believe in Christ, and are united to him by his sanctifying Spirit, will share the privileges of Israelites. There is room in the church, and in heaven, for all who seek the blessings of that new covenant of which Christ is Mediator.

The land and the city where the Lord dwells

This chapter describes the portion of land belonging to each tribe.

In gospel times, all things are made new.

Much of the prophecy is expressed through symbols and numbers.

God has used this manner of speech to communicate mysteries whose meaning will not become fully clear until the proper time.

Yet access to Christ's church—both in its present struggle and its final triumph—is freely open through faith from every side.

Christ has opened the kingdom of heaven to all who believe.

Whoever desires may come and freely receive the water of life and the fruit of the tree of life.

The Lord is there, within his church, near to his people whenever they call upon him.

This is also true of every genuine Christian.

Wherever a soul has a living principle of divine grace, it can truly be said: The Lord is there.

May we be found among the citizens of that holy city.

May we live in a way worthy of that citizenship and enjoy the Lord's presence in life, in death and forever.
classic_reading:
[Ezek.48.1]
Chapter 48
Here is a description of the several portions of the land belonging to each tribe. In gospel times, behold all things are become new. Much is wrapped up in emblems and numbers. This method God has used to state mysterious truths in his word, not to be more clearly revealed till the proper time and season. But into the church of Christ, both in its state of warfare and triumph, there is free access by faith, from every side. Christ has opened the kingdom of heaven for all believers. Whoever will, may come, and take of the water of life, of the tree of life, freely. The Lord is there, in his church, to be nigh unto them in all they call upon him for. This is true of every real Christian; whatever soul has in it a living principle of grace, it may truly be said, The Lord is there. May we be found citizens of this holy city, and act agreeably to that character; and have the benefit of the Lord's presence with us, in life, in death, and for evermore.
